question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed generic ordered configuration-authority model as its core host-management contract?
rationale: The proposal defines durable product and architecture semantics for ownership, persistence, writes, startup, reload, inspection, and compatibility that cannot be selected through mechanical review.

options.title: Continue generic RFC
options.body: Refine the proposed model using the Lobster migration and prototype as concrete acceptance evidence.

options.title: Narrow the seam
options.body: Specify only a smaller host-managed configuration interface for the demonstrated deployment need.

options.title: Retain external overlays
options.body: Keep deployment-owned configuration enforcement outside OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Continue generic RFC
recommendation.body: Refine the proposed model using the Lobster migration and prototype as concrete acceptance evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the proposal and have the strongest adjacent RFC history, while final acceptance remains with core architecture owners.
